newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea won ends up, supported by BOK intervention.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea won ends up, supported by BOK intervention.

text.p: Central bank intervention and the U.S. dollar's retreat against the Japanese yen in world markets sent South Korean won to a higher close versus the U.S. unit on Tuesday, dealers said.
The won ended trading at 862.80 after opening the day at an intra-day low of 865.00. It touched a high of 860.00.

Dealers said the Bank of Korea (BOK) sold dollars shortly after the day's trading started. It later offered to sell dollars in forward trading. "The central bank's intervention was much stronger than traders had earlier expected, and this affected dollar buying later on," said one dealer.
The central bank refused to comment.
"The won had so far been pressured by the trade deficit and the yen's weakness. But now the dollar/yen is easing and this makes traders rethink their positions," said another dealer.
Dealers saw there was a chance the local currency would move sideways in narrow ranges for the time being, cautious about the central bank and yen's short-term outlook.
They foresaw the won's base mid-rate for Wednesday at 862.40 won, compared to Tuesday's 864.40.
